description: Database checks for mappings into EF Core entities: DatabaseAssert.SavesRoundTrip maps, saves and reads back an entity inside a rolled-back transaction and reports every value the database changed (database defaults that replace a copied false or 0, truncated text, rounded numbers), and DatabaseAssert.ModelMatchesDatabase compares the EF Core model's columns, nullability, maximum lengths and defaults with the real schema (SQL Server and SQLite).
releaseNotes:
## 1.10.0 (unreleased)

`ReverseMap()` for enum maps, plus database-level checks, honest acknowledgements and version safety from adopting 1.9 in a large scaffolded codebase.

**Upgrading:**
- New warnings can appear on existing code: CM0034 (a copied `false` or `0` replaced by a database default) and CM0035 (a `[MapReviewed]` entry that acknowledges nothing, such as entries added for the 1.9.0 CM0028 false positive). With warnings as errors, check before upgrading.
- ConventionMapper.Testing now fails when the mapper was generated by another major or minor version of the generator. Reference the same version of both packages.

### Runtime package
- **`ReverseMap()` for enum maps:** `ConvertUsingEnumMapping(o => o.MapValue(Color.Purple, ColorDto.Violet).ReverseMap())` also creates `ColorDto` → `Color` with the same matching (by name, case-insensitive or by value) and every override inverted. `ReverseMap(fallback: Color.Red)` sets the reverse map's fallback (a forward `Fallback` can't be inverted). Two overrides onto the same value can't be inverted: validation reports it and mapping that value back throws. `ReverseMap()` on the map itself, before or after `ConvertUsingEnumMapping`, inverts the mapping too, matching AutoMapper.Extensions.EnumMapping.

### Source generator
- **CM0034 (warning):** a create method writes a non-nullable `bool`, number or enum of an EF Core entity whose column has a database default other than the CLR default (`HasDefaultValueSql("((1))")`, `HasDefaultValue(1)`). EF Core leaves a property holding `false` or `0` out of the insert, so the row silently gets the default instead of the copied value. Fix by making the property nullable or configuring `HasSentinel`, or acknowledge it with `[MapReviewed]`. Strings, `DateTime`, `Guid`, nullable members, keys, members with `HasSentinel` and defaults equal to the CLR default (`((0))`) are not reported.
- **CM0035 (warning):** a `[MapReviewed]` entry on a method or the mapper class that silences nothing: no method that uses it (the method, methods inheriting it through `[MapInherit]`, or every method for the class) writes the member as a key, a database-generated value, a navigation, a column with a database default or a string that can be too long. Stale acknowledgements would hide a future problem.
- **CM0036 (info):** a create method copies a value that can be null into a nullable entity member whose column has a database default; EF Core leaves null out of the insert, so the default is stored. Often intended, so information; acknowledge it with `[MapReviewed("X", For = ReviewKind.DatabaseDefault)]`.
- **`[MapReviewed(..., For = ReviewKind.Key)]`**: an acknowledgement can name the kinds of warning it covers (`Key`, `GeneratedValue`, `Navigation`, `DatabaseDefault`, `Length`; `All` by default, as before), so acknowledging a key write no longer hides a length problem on the same member. CM0035 tracks each attribute and its kinds.
- **`[MapReviewed(..., Reason = "...")]`**: the data-flow report lists every acknowledgement with its kinds and reason in a new "Acknowledged with [MapReviewed]" section.
- The EF model reader also reads `HasDefaultValue(...)` and `HasSentinel(...)`.
- Scaffolded-model tests: code shaped exactly like `dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold` output, with every diagnostic of a typical row copy listed, so false positives on scaffolded models fail the build of the library.

### Testing
- **Version check:** `MapperAssert` methods that read generated metadata (`WriteSets`, `Lineage`, `GeneratedCode`) fail with both versions when the generator's major or minor version differs from ConventionMapper.Testing's, instead of failing in confusing ways.
- `SampleDataOptions.Clone()`: an independent copy, to add values for one run.

### ConventionMapper.Testing.EntityFrameworkCore (new package)
- **`DatabaseAssert.SavesRoundTrip(context, map, source)`**: maps, inserts inside a rolled-back transaction, reads back, and fails for every value the database changed: a default that replaced a copied `false` (CM0034 in action), cut text, rounded numbers; failed inserts carry the database's message.
- **`DatabaseAssert.AllMappersSaveRoundTrip(context, typeof(Mappings))`**: `SavesRoundTrip` for every generated create method that returns an entity of the context, with sample data and again with `false` and `0` values (the ones a database default replaces). Foreign keys aren't checked inside the rolled-back transaction, so no rows need seeding; CHECK constraints, NOT NULL and unique indexes stay on, so a value the database rejects still fails.
- **`DatabaseAssert.ModelMatchesDatabase(context)`**: compares the EF Core model's tables and columns (existence, nullability, maximum length on SQL Server, defaults) with the real schema, so a scaffolded model that drifted is found before the generator's warnings mislead. SQL Server and SQLite.
- **`DatabaseAssert.ExportSchema(context, "schema.json")`** and **`ModelMatchesSchema(context, "schema.json")`**: export the real schema once (from a copy of production), commit the file, and check the model against it in every test run, without a database.

### Build
- Running the workflow manually on `main` publishes `<next version>-preview.<run>` packages to nuget.org (unless that version is already released), so changes can be tried in a real codebase before the release tag. Previews are published on request because nuget.org keeps every version.
- A `sqlserver` CI job runs the database checks against a real SQL Server 2022 and is required before packing.
- After a release tag, the workflow opens a pull request merging `main` into every `feature/*` branch that doesn't contain it yet.
- Release checklist in [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/katragvb/Conventionmapper/blob/main/RELEASING.md), including trying the preview in a real codebase before tagging.
- Package validation baselines moved to 1.9.1; the new package validates its API across target frameworks from its first release.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md in this package, or https://github.com/katragvb/Conventionmapper/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
